mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 40% or more of the periods following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 30% or more of the periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) alongside rising real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 35% or more of the periods when both INDPRO and RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Steady growth in real GDP (GDPC1) during a late-cycle expansion signals sustained economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 40% or more of the periods following GDPC1 growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 35% or more of the periods following PAYEMS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.2 million units signals strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 30% or more of the periods when HOUST exceeds 1.2 million, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls, it indicates tightening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 35% or more of the periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized indicates inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as the market anticipates monetary policy responses.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 40% or more of the periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.
